title: Introduce AZ-aware ENI egress proxy, DNS cascade fallback, and upgrade rollback hooks
author: Leah Martinez
release_notes: Adds AZ-aware ephemeral ENI egress proxies for control plane, DNS cascade fallback between resolver sets, and automated rollback hooks for failed control-plane upgrades; Terraform modules and Helm charts updated. No user API changes.
description:
Motivation and summary: We observed a class of private-deployment failures where control-plane egress relied on centralized NAT instances that created single points of failure and noisy neighbor egress behavior during upgrades. This PR introduces an AZ-aware ENI-based egress proxy pattern that attaches ephemeral ENIs into customer subnets, plus a DNS cascade fallback mechanism (primary resolver set in-region, secondary cross-region) and explicit upgrade rollback hooks to restore prior routing and ENI state when healthchecks fail during a control-plane upgrade.

What this changes (single continuous description): Implements a new Terraform module (terraform/modules/az-eni-egress) that allocates per-AZ ENI proxy appliances (small EC2 instances or AMI-based proxies) with associated security groups, IAM role, and per-subnet route table entries. The installer will create route-table hooks that can be atomically swapped during rollout: new-route -> healthcheck -> confirm -> commit. If healthchecks fail, the rollback hook removes ENI routes and restores previous route attachments. Adds opt-in configuration in the installer values (helm/controlplane/values.yaml) to enable AZ_ENI_EGRESS true/false, with sensible defaults enabled for Dedicated/Private tier.

DNS cascade fallback: Adds a resolver set abstraction and two resolver groups: local (primary) and global-fallback (secondary). The control-plane resolver configuration will prefer local resolvers and fall back to the global set when local lookups timeout or NXDOMAIN patterns match (configurable TTL and retry thresholds). Implements resolver chaining in the installer templates and a small sidecar agent (controlplane/dns-fallback-agent) which monitors resolver health and atomically updates /etc/resolv.conf inside the control-plane container group when a failover is required.

Upgrade/rollback tooling: Adds a small orchestration script (hack/upgrade-rollback.sh) used by the installer to perform staged route swaps and ENI promotions during rolling upgrades. The script executes: (1) create new ENI proxies in target AZs, (2) add temporary route entries with lower priority, (3) run healthcheck suite (connectivity, latency, DNS resolution), (4) commit by switching route priority, (5) clean up old ENIs. If any step fails the script triggers rollback: revert route table to previous state, de-assign new ENIs, and emit alerts with a runbook link. The Helm chart includes a post-upgrade hook to call this script when using the helm-based installer.

Terraform and helm changes: - terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/*: new module with main.tf, security group templates, outputs for route IDs and ENI IDs. - installer/helmcharts/controlplane/templates/eni-proxy.yaml: DaemonSet/Deployment template for proxy installation. - installer/helmcharts/controlplane/values.yaml: new config flags and resolver groups. - hack/upgrade-rollback.sh: orchestration script (bash). - docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md: operator doc with config knobs and troubleshooting. - tests/integration/test-eni-rollback.py: small pytest integration test simulating failed healthcheck and asserting routes restored.

Commits (summary): [1/5] terraform: add az-eni-egress module and README - scaffolds resources and outputs. [2/5] helm: add eni-proxy chart fragment and values for resolver groups. [3/5] installer: wire module outputs into controlplane module and add route-swap hooks. [4/5] tooling: add hack/upgrade-rollback.sh and unit tests for rollback logic. [5/5] docs + integration tests: operator guide and pytest for failure case.

Files changed (high-level): terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/main.tf; terraform/modules/az-eni-egress/outputs.tf; installer/helmcharts/controlplane/templates/eni-proxy.yaml; installer/helmcharts/controlplane/values.yaml; installer/controls/route-swap-hook.yaml; hack/upgrade-rollback.sh; docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md; tests/integration/test-eni-rollback.py; charts/values.schema.json (bumped schema).

Testing and CI: Local integration suite was run against a minimal VPC in CI using a small instance type for proxy appliances. CI initially failed in the first run due to a race in route propagation; fix applied in commit 3 and CI re-run. Final CI status: pass (build, terraform-plan, helm-lint, integration-tests).

Review conversation (high-level, single continuous narrative): Ravi: "Can you clarify how the ENI proxies authenticate to AWS APIs and whether we leak IAM credentials under scale?" — Leah: "ENI proxies use an instance-profile IAM role with least privilege; we rotate role association using the installer's role-assignment workflow. Added README section and automated test to validate no long-lived credentials are written to disk." Ana: "We need to ensure rollback doesn't leave dangling route table associations in multi-AZ tests." — Leah: "Added atomic route-swap steps and an explicit finalizer that re-checks route table state; integration test covers this." Marcus: "How does DNS cascade affect latency-sensitive control-plane calls?" — Leah: "Default thresholds are conservative (50ms timeout, 3 retries) and can be disabled; documented trade-offs. Also the agent prefers in-AZ resolvers so long tail is minimized." Several smaller comments addressed (nits on naming, extra logs) and approvals granted by all reviewers.

Security review: Security reviewed IAM policy and SG rules; no high-severity issues found. Added extra egress filtering rules to the proxy SG and documented the minimum port set.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Release plan: staged rollout to Dedicated customers during next maintenance window; changelog entry added.

Operator notes & runbook pointers: docs/privatedeploy/az-eni-egress.md includes a troubleshooting section that covers ENI cleanup, route reconciliation, and how to manually trigger rollback hooks. The hack script emits structured logs for the console and integrates with our alerting topic for automatic paging when rollback activates.
